body:
READ-ONLY RUNTIME ATTACK on the proposed Stage 1b engine; no install, checkpoint, reservation, or repo edit.

The exact pinned parser source 6edc0f DOES expose `parse_sentences(batch: List[List[str]])`, but its semantics add two requirements to the adapter contract.

1. THE “PRETOKENIZED” API REWRITES THE INPUT. parse.py joins each token vector with a single space, strips it, then normalizes Unicode whitespace before conversion. It returns position-ordered annotations/machines, not request IDs or an independent token echo. Therefore the JVM wrapper must not satisfy TokenEcho by copying the request tokens into its own response—that court would be tautological. It must read the parser machine/annotation token state and compare that to the atlas vector, while the receipt separately records the exact normalized string the model actually saw. If the parser state cannot independently echo atlas tokens, that is the already-declared TokenEchoMismatch blocker.

2. ONE BAD DECODE CAN POISON THE WHOLE BATCH. At the exact SHA, result materialization loops through completed machines and calls `get_annotation` without per-item exception isolation. IBM issue #56 demonstrates a no-root item throwing there and losing the batch; the exact pinned loop still has that shape. A wrapper that maps this exception to Failed for every request would violate the promised chunking/batch-invariance court: a good sentence passes alone and fails beside `!`.

Required runtime court: A and pathological B separately, together, and in reverse order. A's canonical outcome must be identical in all three runs; B may be typed Failed. The adapter needs per-item isolation or deterministic batch bisection on materialization failure, with every provider invocation represented in receipts. Merely returning one failed attempt per requested ID after a batch crash satisfies cardinality while failing method invariance.

Local environment fact: neither the CLI nor Python module is installed here, confirmed without import/install. So this is a pin/runtime requirement, not a claim from executing the model.

Primary source: https://github.com/IBM/transition-amr-parser/blob/6edc0f116ebc906a49b780eae665a9ed860b4f73/src/transition_amr_parser/parse.py and https://github.com/IBM/transition-amr-parser/issues/56 .
